title: The docks that fed a city's fortunes
description: Everything that made money in this para came off a ship - jute, tea, coal, engineering goods. The Ghosals built their palace here for a reason, and the old money along these lanes still traces back to the water.

title: Before the airport, an arsenal town
description: Say Dum Dum today and people think of the airport. For most of its history it meant the opposite - barracks, arsenals and parade grounds, one of British India's biggest cantonments, training soldiers for an empire.

title: The warehouses Armenian merchants left behind
description: It was Armenian money that financed the warehouses and trade routes that turned Calcutta into a port. Walk the lanes off the church and you are walking through what is left of that commercial network.

title: What the Ezras built besides synagogues
description: The same family paid for schools, hospitals, markets and public buildings all over the city. Half the nineteenth-century architecture people photograph in this part of town was funded by them.

title: A street named after the city's richest family
description: Ezra Street carries the name of the Baghdadi Jewish merchants who were among the wealthiest people in nineteenth-century Calcutta. Most of the traders working here today have no idea whose street they are on.

title: A road older than Kolkata itself
description: Chitpur Road was here before British Calcutta was. It linked villages and pilgrimage routes long before anyone drew a city on this bend of the river, which makes it one of eastern India's oldest roads still in use.

title: A riverside suburb older than the city
description: Cossipore was already a village on the Hooghly before colonial Calcutta grew out towards it. The garden houses along the river are what is left of that older, slower settlement.

title: Named after an Italian, famous for the Chinese
description: Edward Tiretta was an Italian architect who owned land here in the late 1700s. The name stuck, but the neighbourhood became India's first Chinatown instead - an Italian street known the world over for Chinese food.

title: Where gods begin a journey around the world
description: Every year thousands of idols made in these lanes are crated up and shipped to London, New Jersey, Sydney, Singapore. The Durga you see in a pandal abroad almost certainly started here.

title: Saints and courtesans on the same lane
description: In the nineteenth century this para held wealthy merchant houses and a well-known courtesan quarter side by side - and Ramakrishna Paramahansa was a regular visitor to the ghat and to devotees living in the same lanes.
